body:
N-34 DESIGN, part 5: FOR THE ADVISOR. Three decisions the code cannot settle; the default stands until you answer (yours to overrule).
1. THE PAIR. Default: Creature's twin is HELD (left alone, logged); the owner still sees it in 'Songs without an album' until slice 6. Alternative: make slice 6 part of the repair's first run: merge A into B when the catalogue names both as one recording and no playlist holds both, and DELETE A's kept copy. That is the only way his own example ends and what he expects ('one song'), but it deletes a kept file and changes what is behind a like. The five pairs you held on 14 Nov stay held either way. Read first on the database: do both Creatures sit in a playlist together?
2. THE ONE-TIME RE-DOWNLOAD. Default: accept that every downloaded song that is repaired is fetched again once on Wi-Fi (refAudioKey hashes the byte size, fingerprint.dart:101; proved in the planner). Alternative: hold the repair until the server hands the phone an audio-only key (a hash of the stream; a tag edit never refreshes a copy again): the proper fix of a contract whose comment is wrong today, a server and a phone change, its own item (not created here: the lead numbers it). Slice 4 may show that the music server's id changes on a plain retag, which would make this cost certain.
3. A SINGLE. Default: a catalogue single is its own release (its title as the album, track 1, its own folder), only when no album or EP carries the recording; Singles/ then means 'no album known'. Alternative: a single keeps Singles/ with no album tag, which leaves it in the bucket and contradicts the bucket meaning 'the catalogue does not know it' (the brief said 'Singles is right for a single'; I read the folder as the place for songs with no album, and a single IS an album of one).
THINGS I DID THAT YOU MAY WANT TO FLIP
- Per the ruling N-34 now has needs P2-25 [d] in items.json (with a Why), and order.json carries P2-25 forward to just before N-34 (position 7): a drag carries needs, and P2-25's own note says 'fix before you try the app on your phone'. The other way is to move N-34 behind P2-25 (position ~30).
- Audit row B-133 (the cover finder accepts a live version and any name that folds to nothing; the keeper never asks the catalogue for an imported song); B-110's 'lands in' also names N-34 slice 3. B-133 was the next free audit number on 15 Nov: if another PR took it, renumber.
- RELEASE-CANDIDATE 4b gets a gate: slices 1 to 3 in the FIRST public image, so no stranger ever makes a bucket; slice 5 is for installs that hold songs kept before them (the owner's).
- PROPOSED row N-34 points at the design and says it needs P2-25.
Nothing is built, marked or walked. The item stays todo.
